requirements.summary: The March test passes a fault-free array and finds stuck-at-0 and stuck-at-1 cells, also when the memory stalls.
When spare rows and columns can cover every fault of the main array, the allocation covers them: with rows, with columns, with both, and with a row that only a spare row can repair.
When no choice of spare rows and columns covers the faults, the result is unrepairable and no fuse is programmed.
A spare row or column with a fault is not used; faults on spares alone need no repair.
Fuses are programmed once and only gain bits; a reset loads them, the test after the repair passes, and a later fault fails it without another repair.
A reset in the middle of a test abandons it; the next test gives the same result.
